summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted with a vaso-occlusive pain crisis involving her chest, hips, and knees, following two weeks of respiratory symptoms and dehydration. She was treated with IV hydration, supplemental oxygen, and IV narcotics. On the second hospital day, she developed transient hypoxia and a chest X-ray revealed moderate pulmonary edema and new small pleural effusions, prompting discontinuation of IV fluids; she improved with autodiuresis. Due to persistent leukocytosis, fever, and cough, she was treated empirically with levofloxacin for suspected atypical pneumonia, with resolution of symptoms. Vitamin B12 supplementation was initiated for low-normal levels. She was transitioned to oral pain medication, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged. Blood cultures were negative, and a urine culture showed gram-positive bacteria without clinical signs of UTI.
